original.target_description: Study 3: US Prolific dental-treatment choice experiment; serial and parallel mediation involving small self and human imperfection are both reported.

n.sample_role: Participants; printed count is recruitment, not an explicitly documented critical-model analytic sample.
n.exclusions: Final exclusions and model-specific missingness are not established in the supplied main article. Sampling details and full analyses are referred to the unsupplied SI Appendix.
n.location: Materials and Methods, Study 3, canonical line 81; Results, Study 3, canonical line 40; SI referral line 65
n.quote: Additional methodological information, sampling details, and full analyses are provided in SI Appendix. ... US-based participants (n = 377; Mage = 37.9 y, 204 female and 11 nonbinary) were recruited on Prolific in exchange for money and were randomly assigned to one of the two God salience conditions.

es.quote: Supporting our theorizing, the indirect effect of God salience on algorithm acceptance with small self as the proximal mediator and belief in human imperfection as the distal mediator was significant (B = 0.03, CI95% = [0.0005, 0.0817]). Of note, a model with small self and belief in human imperfection as parallel mediators resulted in an insignificant indirect effect of small self (B = 0.03; CI95% = [−0.1165, 0.2101]) and a significant effect of belief in human imperfection (B = 0.07; CI95% = [0.0058, 0.2002]).
